subject: maths
title: Model Question Paper 2
meta: Time: 2½ hours · Maximum marks: 85 · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Section A: questions 1–17 are MCQs (1 mark each); questions 18–27 have two parts of 1 mark each; question 28 is a case study with five 1-mark questions.
Section B: questions 29–37 carry 2 marks, 38–42 carry 3 marks and 43–44 carry 5 marks.
Every answer shows the working. Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: 4x² − 9y² is equal to —
questions.work:
4x² − 9y² = (2x)² − (3y)², a difference of two squares.
a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b), so 4x² − 9y² = (2x + 3y)(2x − 3y).

questions.q: The graph of y = −3 is a line —
questions.work:
On y = −3 every point has y-coordinate −3, e.g. (0, −3), (5, −3).
All the points are at the same height, so the line is parallel to the x-axis, 3 units below it.

questions.q: Which of the following is a quadratic equation?
questions.work:
A quadratic equation can be written as ax² + bx + c = 0 with a ≠ 0.
x² − 5x + 2 = 0 has degree 2. x³ + x = 1 has degree 3, 2x + 3 = 0 degree 1, and x + 1/x is not a polynomial.

questions.q: An A.P. has sum of first three terms 18 and common difference 4. The A.P. is —
questions.work:
First three terms: a, a + 4, a + 8. Sum 3a + 12 = 18 ⇒ a = 2.
The A.P. is 2, 6, 10, …

questions.q: The simple interest on ₹2,500 for 2 years 6 months at 6% per annum is —
An article costs ₹5,000 cash; under a plan the buyer pays ₹1,000 down. The balance owed is —
questions.work: Balance = cash price − cash down = 5000 − 1000 = ₹4,000.

questions.q: A chord of a circle equals its radius. The angle it subtends at a point on the major arc is —
questions.work:
The chord and two radii form an equilateral triangle, so the central angle is 60°.
Angle on the major arc = ½ × 60° = 30°.

questions.q: The number of tangents that can be drawn to a circle from a point inside it is —
questions.work: Every line through an interior point cuts the circle in two points, so it is a secant. No tangent is possible: 0.

questions.q: A triangle with AB + AC = 5 cm and BC = 6 cm —
questions.work: The sum of two sides must be greater than the third: AB + AC must exceed BC. 5 < 6, so it cannot be constructed.

questions.q: If the x-coordinate of a point is zero, the point lies —
questions.work: x = distance from the y-axis. x = 0 means the point is on the y-axis, e.g. (0, 5).

questions.q: The area of a square of perimeter 44 cm is —
questions.work: Side = 44 ÷ 4 = 11 cm. Area = 11² = 121 cm².

questions.q: The surface area of a cube of side 27 cm is —
Two cubes of edge 12 cm are joined end to end. The surface area of the resulting cuboid is —
If sin θ + sin²θ = 1, then cos²θ + cos⁴θ is —
questions.work:
sin θ = 1 − sin²θ = cos²θ.
So cos²θ + cos⁴θ = sin θ + sin²θ = 1.

questions.q: A 30 m ladder touches a wall at a height of 15 m. The angle it makes with the ground is —
The mean of the first five prime numbers is —
questions.work:
First five primes: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11. Sum = 28.
Mean = 28/5 = 5.6.

questions.q: A die is thrown once. The probability of getting a number between 2 and 6 is —
questions.work:
Numbers strictly between 2 and 6: 3, 4, 5 — 3 outcomes out of 6.
P = 3/6 = 1/2.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, match the columns or true/false).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) The HCF of x³ + 1 and x² − 1 is ________. (ii) (2x² + 5)² − (2x² − 5)² = ________.
questions.answer:
(i) x³ + 1 = (x + 1)(x² − x + 1) and x² − 1 = (x + 1)(x − 1); common factor x + 1, so HCF = x + 1.
(ii) (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab = 4 × 2x² × 5 = 40x².

questions.q: Write True or False: (i) The point (4, 3) lies on 3x + 7y = 27. (ii) The graph of y = −3 is parallel to the x-axis.
questions.answer:
(i) False: 3(4) + 7(3) = 33 ≠ 27.
(ii) True: every point on it has y = −3.

questions.q: Match: (i) The roots of 2x² + x − 6 = 0 are ____ (ii) The roots of x² − 3x + 3 = 0 are ____ — (A) real and distinct (B) real and equal (C) not real
Fill in the blanks: (i) The 20th term from the end of 3, 8, 13, …, 253 is ____. (ii) If a = 5, l = 45 and the sum is 400, the number of terms is ____.

Aarush earns ₹45,000 a month: 50% on the household, 20% on himself, 20% on his children and the rest is saved. Fill in: (i) his total monthly expenditure ____ (ii) his expenditure on his children ____.
A TV costs ₹20,000 cash, or ₹5,000 down and ₹15,500 after 4 months. Fill in: (i) interest ____ (ii) rate of interest ____ p.a.
Fill in the blanks: (i) In cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, ∠DBC = 55° and ∠BAC = 45°; then ∠BCD = ____. (ii) The angle subtended at the centre by a semicircle is a ____ angle.
Fill in the blanks: (i) PT is a tangent at P to a circle with centre O and ∠QPT = 60° (PQ a chord); ∠POQ = ____. (ii) TP and TQ are tangents and ∠POQ = 110°; ∠PTQ = ____.
questions.answer:
(i) ∠OPT = 90°, so ∠OPQ = 30° = ∠OQP; ∠POQ = 180° − 60° = 120°. (The central angle is twice the tangent-chord angle.)
(ii) ∠PTQ = 360° − 90° − 90° − 110° = 70°.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) If the mode of 12, 16, 19, 16, x, 12, 16, 19, 12 is 16, then x = ____. (ii) If the median of a data is 24 and each item is increased by 2, the new median is ____.
questions.answer:
(i) 12 occurs 3 times and 16 three times; for 16 to be the only mode it must occur more, so x = 16.
(ii) Adding 2 to every item adds 2 to the median: 26.

questions.q: A box has 3 blue, 4 white and 5 red balls. Fill in (any two): (i) P(white) (ii) P(blue) (iii) P(red) (iv) P(neither white nor red).
questions.answer:
Total = 12.
(i) 4/12 = 1/3. (ii) 3/12 = 1/4. (iii) 5/12. (iv) Neither white nor red means blue: 3/12 = 1/4.

questions.q: The distance between the school and the hospital is —

questions.work: C(5, −1): x positive, y negative ⇒ quadrant IV.

sections.passage: A town map is drawn on a grid with the bus stand at the origin. The school is at A(2, 3), the hospital at B(8, 11) and the market at C(5, −1). Distances are in kilometres.

questions.q: Find the LCM of P(x) = x³ + 2x² − 3x and Q(x) = 2x³ + 5x² − 3x.
questions.answer:
P(x) = x(x² + 2x − 3) = x(x + 3)(x − 1).
Q(x) = x(2x² + 5x − 3) = x(2x² + 6x − x − 3) = x(2x − 1)(x + 3).
LCM = every factor with its highest power = x(x + 3)(x − 1)(2x − 1).

or.answer:
Square both sides: (x + 1/x)² = 4.
x² + 2 × x × (1/x) + 1/x² = 4 ⇒ x² + 2 + 1/x² = 4.
So x² + 1/x² = 4 − 2 = 2.

questions.q: Solve 3x − y = 5 and 4x + 3y = 11.
questions.answer:
From the first, y = 3x − 5.
Substitute: 4x + 3(3x − 5) = 11 ⇒ 13x − 15 = 11 ⇒ x = 2.
y = 3(2) − 5 = 1.
Solution: x = 2, y = 1.

questions.q: Find the nature of the roots of 2x² + x − 6 = 0 and find them.
Find the sum of the first 20 terms of 16, 11, 6, 1, −4, …
A car bought for ₹5,50,000 on 1.1.2025 depreciates by 15% in the first year and 10% in every year after. Find its value on 31.12.2027.
A radio costs ₹1,000 cash or ₹400 down and ₹630 after 6 months. Find the rate of interest.
questions.answer:
Balance = ₹600; interest = 630 − 600 = ₹30 for ½ year.
30 = 600 × R × ½/100 = 3R ⇒ R = 10% per annum.

questions.q: In a circle with centre O, ∠BAC = 35°. Find ∠OBC.
ABC is an isosceles triangle with AB = AC, and XAY is the tangent at A to its circumcircle. Show that XY ∥ BC.
questions.answer:
By the alternate segment theorem, ∠XAB = ∠ACB.
AB = AC ⇒ ∠ABC = ∠ACB. So ∠XAB = ∠ABC.
These are alternate angles made by AB with XY and BC, so XY ∥ BC.

questions.q: Write the steps to divide a line segment of 7 cm internally in the ratio 3 : 4.
questions.answer:
1. Draw AB = 7 cm.
2. Draw a ray AX making an acute angle with AB.
3. With a fixed compass opening, mark 3 + 4 = 7 equal points A₁, …, A₇ on AX.
4. Join A₇B.
5. Through A₃ draw a line parallel to A₇B (copy ∠AA₇B at A₃) meeting AB at P.
6. Then AP : PB = 3 : 4 (AP = 3 cm, PB = 4 cm).

questions.q: Factorise a⁶ − 64b⁶.
questions.answer:
a⁶ − 64b⁶ = (a³)² − (8b³)² = (a³ − 8b³)(a³ + 8b³).
a³ − 8b³ = a³ − (2b)³ = (a − 2b)(a² + 2ab + 4b²).
a³ + 8b³ = a³ + (2b)³ = (a + 2b)(a² − 2ab + 4b²).
So a⁶ − 64b⁶ = (a − 2b)(a + 2b)(a² + 2ab + 4b²)(a² − 2ab + 4b²).

or.answer:
Factorise: a² − 1 = (a − 1)(a + 1); a² − 25 = (a − 5)(a + 5); a² − 4a − 5 = (a − 5)(a + 1); a² + 4a − 5 = (a + 5)(a − 1).
Divide by multiplying with the reciprocal:
[(a − 1)(a + 1)]/[(a − 5)(a + 5)] × [(a + 5)(a − 1)]/[(a − 5)(a + 1)].
Cancel (a + 1) and (a + 5): (a − 1)²/(a − 5)².

questions.q: In an election 75% of the voters cast their votes. The winner got 51% of the votes cast, which was 1530 votes. Find the total number of voters.
questions.answer:
Let there be V voters. Votes cast = 0.75V; winner's votes = 0.51 × 0.75V = 0.3825V.
0.3825V = 1530 ⇒ V = 4000.

questions.q: Chords AB and CD of a circle meet at P. If AP = x + 1, BP = x + 2, CP = x and DP = x + 4, find x.
Two perpendicular paths, each 10 m wide, run through the middle of a 200 m × 150 m park. Find the cost of constructing them at ₹50 per m².
questions.answer:
Path along the length: 200 × 10 = 2000 m². Path along the breadth: 150 × 10 = 1500 m².
Common square 10 × 10 = 100 m² is counted twice.
Area = 2000 + 1500 − 100 = 3400 m². Cost = 3400 × 50 = ₹1,70,000.

questions.q: A man on top of a 120 m tower sees two cars on opposite sides of the tower, in line with its base, at depressions of 60° and 45°. Find the distance between the cars. (√3 = 1.732)
Construct a triangle ABC in which AB = 5 cm, BC = 4.2 cm and the median CD = 3.8 cm.
questions.answer:
D is the midpoint of AB, so BD = 2.5 cm.
1. Construct △BCD: draw BD = 2.5 cm; with centre B radius 4.2 cm and centre D radius 3.8 cm draw arcs meeting at C. Join BC and DC.
2. Produce BD to A so that DA = 2.5 cm (AB = 5 cm).
3. Join AC. △ABC is the required triangle, with median CD = 3.8 cm.

or.q: Draw a circle of radius 3.2 cm and from a point P outside it draw two tangents PQ and PR.
or.answer:
1. Draw a circle with centre O, radius 3.2 cm. Mark a point P outside it (say OP = 6 cm) and join OP.
2. Bisect OP at M.
3. With centre M and radius MO draw a circle cutting the given circle at Q and R.
4. Join PQ and PR; these are the tangents, and PQ = PR.

questions.q: A cylindrical container of diameter 12 cm and height 15 cm is full of ice-cream. It is filled into cones of height 12 cm and diameter 6 cm. How many cones can be filled?
questions.answer:
Cylinder: π × 6² × 15 = 540π.
One cone: ⅓π × 3² × 12 = 36π.
Number = 540π ÷ 36π = 15 cones.
